t: You're at St Pancras Old Church, a Church of England parish church on Pancras Road in Somers Town. It takes its name from Saint Pancras, a Roman citizen who converted to Christianity and was beheaded for his faith at fourteen. Its burial ground holds some remarkable people. William Godwin, the political philosopher, is buried here. Two composers who moved to London lie here too, Johann Christian Bach, youngest son of Johann Sebastian, and Carl Friedrich Abel. The writer and physician John William Polidori, credited by some with creating the vampire genre, is also buried here. So is the sculptor John Flaxman.
